headline: Nvidia turmoil and new AI-chip curbs sink chips; SOX −5.3%, Nasdaq −2.5% into correction
summary: Stocks opened lower and never mounted a recovery: selling built through the afternoon, with the S&P 500 down as much as 2.1% (low 7,400.15) in the final two hours before a small late trim, for its third straight loss. It was broad as well as tech-led — decliners beat advancers about 3.5-to-1 on the NYSE and the Russell 2000 fell 1.9% — while consumer staples (+0.3%) and utilities (+0.2%) were the only sectors to rise and technology (−3.2%) was by far the worst.
drivers: Chip sell-off spreads to all 30 SOX names

Every stock in the semiconductor index fell as Friday's reversal deepened: Micron −7.6%, Intel −7.1%, Lam Research −6.7%, ASML −5.9%, AMD −5.6% and Applied Materials −5.5%, with Marvell and Arm also down 6% or more. A report that SemiAnalysis cut its 2028 AI-accelerator spending forecast by 28% and its 2028 HBM demand estimate by 30% added to the pressure on memory and equipment names.

Nvidia fell 4.1% to about $156 after a CNBC report that its board is not discussing bringing back Jensen Huang and is instead investigating his conduct and hiring a search firm for a new CEO; Treasury Secretary Bessent also urged an outside successor. Down about 12.6% over five sessions, it reports after Tuesday's close, with analysts looking for revenue near $109 billion.
New US curbs on remote AI-chip access

The Commerce Department issued a rule closing a route that let Chinese firms rent advanced Nvidia-class computing in third-country data centers, adding license requirements for advanced chip exports to Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia and Brazil. AI-infrastructure names fell with chips: Dell −7.0%, Super Micro −6.9%, Nebius −7.6%, CoreWeave −6.1%, and Alphabet, Amazon and Meta lost between 2.4% and 4.1%.
Defensive rotation as yields and oil ease

Money moved into staples and other steady names (Tyson Foods rose about 7% on a profit beat and upbeat 2027 outlook; Coca-Cola and McDonald's gained), while the 10-year yield slipped about 4bp to 5.12% as WTI fell 3.2% to $85.72 on surplus forecasts from the IEA and Goldman. Fed Chair Warsh said disappointing AI returns could slow growth and lift unemployment, but a December hike stays about 96% priced.
week: The week starts with the S&P 500 down 1.9% and the Nasdaq down 2.5%, leaving the Nasdaq more than 10% below its Oct 6 record close (a correction) and the SOX up about 43% for 2026 versus a 107% gain at its June peak; the 10-year yield remains above 5% after last week's jump on hot inflation data.
watch: Next: Nvidia's third-quarter results and Home Depot on Tue Nov 17, Fed minutes and Anthropic's IPO pricing (reportedly six times oversubscribed) on Wed Nov 18, Walmart on Thu Nov 19, and the Fed meeting on Dec 8–9.
